Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:60083
Court No. - 14

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11275 of 2023
Applicant :- Avinash Patel @ Harsh
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Rinku Verma,Aakash Srivastava,Raj Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.Learned AGA informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter along with upto date case diary and the charge sheet in this case has already been submitted.

2. Heard Shri Rinku Verma, learned counsel for the accused/applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Avinash Patel @ Harsh for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 0289of 2023, under Sections 376(2) (N) IPC, Police Station Ramsanehi Ghat, District Barabanki, during trial.
4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.

The First Information Report of this case has been lodged by the victim herself on 28.7.2023 at Police Station Ramsanehi Ghat, District Barabanki against the applicant Avinash Patel @ Harsh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 alleging therein that the applicant is remotely related to her and earlier taken her to his home and kept there for about a month and in this period he has committed sexual assault on her many times and when she resisted, he lured the victim/ informant by extending false promise of marriage and thereafter he visited her house and made sexual relations with her many times and when she insisted to marry her, he refused to marry.

In her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. she fortified the same allegations with the improvement that she also got pregnant and some medicine was administered by the applicant to her, as a result of which the fetus was aborted.

5. Highlighting the above facts, it is vehemently submitted that the applicant and the victim were studying in the same School and they were having love affair and sexual relations between them were established with the free wish, will and consent of the prosecutrix and there was no element of false compromise of marriage.
6.

Elaborating further it is submitted that the prosecutrix was admittedly of 22 years of age at the relevant date and time of the incident and she was having sufficient intellect to understand her welfare and the allegation of establishing sexual relations on the pretext of false promise of marriage has been carved out subsequently while there was no such compromise ever extended by the applicant.

Reliance in this regard has been placed by learned counsel for the applicant on the judgements of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra and another, reported in (2019)9 SCC 608 and Deepak Gulati Vs. State of Haryana,
reported in (2013)7 SCC 675, wherein a distinction has been made between the breach of promise of marriage and establishing sexual relations by extending false promise of marriage.

sentences.text: 7. It is also submitted that sexual activity between the applicant and the victim was a consensual act of two adults and the same can never be termed as 'sexual assault' or 'rape'.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 29.7.2023 and he is not having any criminal history.

Charge sheet in this matter has already been submitted and there is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

8. Learned AGA on the other hand submits that on the basis of false promise of marriage physical relations have been established by the applicant with the victim and therefore he is not entitled to be released on bail.

9. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that it appears to be an admitted case that even after the initial establishment of sexual relations which as per the victim were made against her will by the applicant, the sexual relations were continuously established by the applicant subsequently and it is stated by the prosecutrix that the said physical relations were in lieu of the false promise of marriage extended by the applicant, while the defence of the applicant appears to be that the applicant and victim were studying in the same School and they were having love affair and sexual relations between them were established with free wish, will and consent of the prosecutrix and there was no element of false promise of marriage.

It is submitted on behalf of the applicant that the sexual activity taken place between the applicant and the victim was a consensual act of the two adults and these disputed questions could only be decided by the trial court after providing an opportunity to the parties to led evidence.
Avinash Patel @ Harsh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

2 10.

Having regard to the fact that the applicant is in jail in this case since 29.7.2023,he is not having any criminal history and keeping in view the law laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar and Deepak Gulati (supra) coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix was major at the date and time of the incident, the facility of bail in the considered opinion of this Court may safely be extended to the applicant.

The bail application moved on behalf of the applicant is, thus,
allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Avinash Patel @ Harsh involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
13. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
14. Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Muk  Avinash Patel @ Harsh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
